A wallet that has PROVEN ownership can no longer be named by a third party: an unsigned, unauthenticated POST /api/v1/bounty/reports naming a verified wallet is refused with HTTP 401 {"code": "WALLET_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED", "message_to_sign": ...}. Two ways to attribute a filing to a verified wallet: (a) field `signature` = EIP-191 personal_sign over the deterministic filing message, or (b) an authenticated session (JWT / evt_ API key) whose user owns the profile. A valid signature on a not-yet-verified wallet verifies it as a side effect, so ONE signed filing locks the identity for good.

The message is deterministic so you can produce it offline: GET /api/v1/bounty/filing-message?wallet_address=<addr>&title=<title> returns it; it is "EventTrader Bug Bounty Report\n\nWallet: <addr lower>\nTitle-SHA256: <sha256(title.strip())>\n\nThis signature does not authorize any blockchain transactions." Replay is bounded by the title hash + the 24h duplicate gate: a captured signature can only re-file the same title, which is rejected.
